palette.notes: Clip3 is real footage, clip1 mixes Smash 3D with real sprite scenes, clip2 is fan art (ignored). Sprites: flat fills plus one darker shade, warm pastels. Backdrops carry the colour: a screen of yellow sunflowers, magenta or blue radial glows, a grey-white flashback, a mauve banded sea.

lighting: No light on sprites at all; mood is set by swapping the whole backdrop: concentric radial glow rings (magenta for menace, blue for a sacred moment with a single vertical light beam), a near-monochrome grey-white flashback room, a sunset-banded sea.
silhouette: Round heads about as big as the body, stubby limbs, clean dark 1px outline all round; characters told apart by one feature (Lucas's blond bowl cut, Kumatora's pink hair, cowboy hats in the funeral crowd). Readable even when the sprite is 12-16 px tall in a wide shot.

motion.timing: No metrics file: describe only. Bespoke cutscene animations; comedy and drama rely on pauses and repeated gags that escalate. In the footage most frames are still, posed characters with the backdrop doing the moving (rings pulse, waves scroll).

texture: Flat pastel fills on characters with a soft dark oval contact shadow under each sprite; backgrounds are banded, wavy or patterned (layered wave stripes, radial rings, dense flower tiles) and animate as the battle and story backdrops.
camera: Top-down 3/4 for exploration with mostly locked frames; battles in first person against distorted animated backgrounds. Cutscenes hold wide on a static stage and let the characters move inside it.
sound: Combo hits are timed to each enemy's music beat; the main theme is simple enough to play with one finger.

acting.enters: Characters arrive in small walk-ons; at the funeral the mourners stand in a loose ring with backs to camera and the hero walks up into the middle.
acting.acts: Comic and sad timing from a beat of stillness, then a short sharp reaction; dialogue boxes carry the emotion while the sprite barely moves. Running gags come back each time a bit sillier.
acting.exits: Walk off mid-scene or simply stop being in frame, letting an empty backdrop (an empty sea, a white flash) land the moment.
acting.depth: Extreme scale for emotion: Lucas tiny alone in a screen of sunflowers; mourners from behind in front frame the hero; party small at the bottom under a huge boss machine.

techniques: running gag that escalates each time it returns
flat unshaded pastel sprites with 1px dark outline and an oval contact shadow
radial glow-ring backdrop recoloured per mood (magenta threat, blue sacred)
whole-scene monochrome wash for a flashback
tiny hero in a huge field of one colour for loneliness
foreground figures seen from behind framing the hero
feel: flat pastel actors + loud single-colour backdrop + beat of stillness before the gag = warm deadpan comedy that can turn sad
for_fred: Make Fred a running gag: he exits, comes back later doing the same bit slightly sillier each time, and once appears tiny alone in a big empty field of colour while Robert talks. Hold still a beat before every reaction, and change the backdrop (radial glow ring in a new colour) instead of animating Fred more.
